task_type: public product design, CMS control and release
requested_outcome: Every public VII discovery world has a distinctive, image-led landing experience at the quality level of the approved spa landing, while retaining fast, simple search and separate CMS control.
natural_destination: The public VII world routes and the VII Content Studio in production.
authorization_boundary: Implementation, verification, pushing and production publication are authorized by the active conversation. No new third-party purchases, invented media, or unrelated product redesign is authorized.

lesson_bundle.reason: The request covers an entire route family and production publication.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Verify every route at its natural destination on desktop and mobile, not just one implementation example.

lesson_bundle.reason: Image-led heroes and horizontal controls commonly regress on small and low-height screens.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Require live 390px, low-height, overflow and interaction checks.

lesson_bundle.reason: Each world includes search, quick links, cards and slider controls.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Every visible control must match its enabled state and complete a real route.

lesson_bundle.reason: Adir explicitly requires separate backend control for each world.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Require editable world identity, content and images with preview, save, publish and persistence evidence.

lesson_bundle.reason: The visible landing content must be managed rather than hard-coded only.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Require validated, permissioned content sources and public reflection for the whole world family.

lesson_bundle.reason: Several world pages are already approved and must not lose search, results or specialized flows.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Preserve existing routes, data, results, SEO and unique corporate and gift-card experiences.

lesson_bundle.reason: All target surfaces are Hebrew-first public pages and admin controls.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Verify the approved Hebrew font and no serif or fallback flash across the affected family.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Only hourly rooms and providers are improved while another generic world page remains.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Inventory all public discovery worlds before implementation and classify already-unique pages explicitly.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: A route matrix covers home, spa, events, hourly, providers, attractions, trails, activities, corporate and gift card.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Every page becomes the same copied spa template with different text.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Use a shared accessible structure with a distinct composition, palette, copy and verified media story for each world.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Desktop and mobile captures show recognizably different world identities without sacrificing consistency.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The new visuals exist in code but cannot be managed from the admin system.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Add one managed landing source per discovery world and reuse the versioned Content Studio workflow.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Admin edit, validation, preview, save, publish and reload are exercised for representative worlds.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The landing looks better but search, results, speed or indexing regresses.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Keep search and result components intact, use optimized images and run route, build, performance and SEO regressions.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Search interactions, result anchors, metadata, build and route tests pass after the visual change.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The source branch is pushed but the public site is described as updated without deployment evidence.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Separate candidate evidence from exact production evidence and report publication only after opening the live release.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: The exact deployed release and every changed public URL are opened and visually verified.

affected_family: shared world hero and quick-search components
Hebrew, English, Russian and French message catalogs
loading, empty, error and published states

midpoint_gate.trigger: After the shared hero model and first two currently-generic worlds render locally, before extending to attractions and trails.
checks: Hourly and providers look distinct from each other and from spa
Existing search and results still work
Representative CMS defaults and validation are visible
390px first screens contain a clear title, image and next action

attack_questions: Can any public discovery world still be mistaken for an unfinished generic template?
Can an editor change one world's hero without changing another or editing code?
Does any image imply an unverified business, place or experience?
Do search, cards, sliders, metadata or results fail after the shared-component change?
Is any production claim based only on a build, commit or deployment queue?
adversarial_close.natural_destination_evidence: Exact candidate screenshots and interactions for every affected public route and admin control, followed by exact production URLs after deployment.
adversarial_close.affected_family_evidence: Automated route and unit tests plus desktop, 390px mobile and low-height visual checks for the entire route matrix.

effectiveness.baseline: Spa, corporate and gift card already have distinctive openings; hourly and providers use a generic landing, while attractions and trails use text-only hero treatments.
effectiveness.target: No generic discovery-world opening remains, all new landing controls are manageable, and the whole affected family passes release checks without a second route-specific repair.
